stories.title: Michigan Democrats prepare for a second trifecta
stories.summary: Michigan Democrats secured a legislative trifecta, regaining full control of the state House and Senate, along with the governor's office. House Minority Leader Ranjeev Puri (D-Canton) is expected to continue leading House Democrats, with the party holding more than a one-vote majority in the upcoming session.

inputFacts.title: Michigan Democrats prepare for a second trifecta
inputFacts.summary: Michigan Democrats have regained full control of the state Legislature and governor’s office following election night wins, expanding their Senate majority and flipping multiple House seats. The party aims to advance policies like gun safety and clean energy with a stronger majority, learning from their previous trifecta period. Leadership transitions and new members will shape the upcoming legislative session.

stories.title: El-Sayed claims victory, wins historic U.S. Senate race
stories.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, former Wayne County and Detroit health director, won Michigan's open U.S. Senate seat, becoming the nation's first Muslim U.S. senator. He defeated Republican Mike Rogers in a hard-fought race, campaigning on a progressive platform focused on healthcare, the environment, and economic issues.

inputFacts.title: Why are flags at half-staff today? Michigan honors late representative
inputFacts.summary: Michigan Governor Gretchen Whitmer ordered U.S. and state flags to be flown at half-staff on November 5, 2026, to honor the late Jack Kirksey. Kirksey, a former state representative and mayor of Livonia, passed away on October 13 at the age of 97.

inputFacts.title: What Michigan election results mean for data centers, DTE, clean energy
inputFacts.summary: Democrats retained control of Michigan's governor's office and state Senate while gaining the House majority, enabling potential advancements in clean energy and environmental protections. The Michiganders for Money Out of Politics ballot initiative banning utility political spending passed with 81% support, while a constitutional convention measure failed. Abdul El-Sayed's Senate victory could influence federal data center regulations, and new leaders like Eli Savit pledged to continue utility ratepayer advocacy. Ballot initiatives like Proposal 2 and Ann Arbor's Proposition E had mixed outcomes, with the latter failing to establish a municipal energy utility.

inputFacts.title: Detroiters have until Nov. 6 to apply for this property tax reduction
inputFacts.summary: The Homeowners Property Exemption can reduce or eliminate 2025 and 2026 property taxes for Detroit residents. Applications must be submitted by November 6.

inputFacts.title: El-Sayed cited Islamic faith with this phrase. What it means
inputFacts.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, who recently won Michigan's U.S. Senate race, gained attention for using Arabic phrases like 'Inshallah' and 'Alhamdulillah' in his victory speech. Experts note that his public embrace of his Islamic faith reflects the state's diverse cultural fabric and history.

inputFacts.title: El-Sayed calls Vance habibi in victory speech. What does it mean?
inputFacts.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed used the Arabic term 'habibi' to refer to Vice President JD Vance during his election night victory speech. El-Sayed, who will become the first Muslim U.S. senator after defeating Mike Rogers, used the term to highlight the irony of Vance swearing him into office.
